liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Johnny B. Goode** (2 reviews): Johnny B. Goode closed set two, following Truckin' with no cut between them; Johnny B. Goode was the last song played before the band left the stage [22][28]
- **Road Runner** (1 review): Road Runner, Comes a Time and Hand Jive are the older numbers later-era followers will want [26]
- **Feel Like a Stranger** (1 review): Stranger opened set two at huge length, with monster playing from Phil [24]
- **Jam** (1 review): The jam leading into Drums is especially sweet [30]
- **Comes a Time** (1 review): Comes a Time was poignant and close to perfect, followed by an abrupt ending [24]

## The recordings

- **gd86-03-31.aud.eD.13463.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 18 songs; 128 min; rated 4.08/5 by 12 [1]. Said about its sound: On this board source Jerry's notes pop out all over the place; reviewer calls it average [30]
- **gd1986-03-31.156189.akgc422.davis-murtha-holbrook.flac2448**: source not stated; 18 songs; 127 min [2]. Said about its sound: A grinding PA sound, thought to be Weir's rig distorting, runs through the recording whenever the band plays [2]
- **gd1986-03-31.177724.sbd.eaton.miller.repatch.flac1648**: soundboard; 17 songs; 129 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]
- **gd1986-03-31.nakcm304.suraci.sbeok.79912.flac16**: source not stated; 17 songs; 125 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [7]

## Around the show

- The band chose not to reward the bottle-throwing with an encore [21]
- The next night, fans outside signed a huge banner apologizing to Billy for the bottle incident [22]
- Outside, an old man held up cardboard displaying photos from an earlier show, not selling them; the NCAA finals were on TV [23]
- Thousands of confused fans poured into the street after the sudden end; the cause was learned the next day [24]
- Reviewer recalls what seemed like rain inside the Civic Center and the show ending early, leaving crowds wandering Providence [27]
- A beer bottle through Billy's kick drum cut the show short; after Johnny B. Goode the band left [28]
- A bottle thrown from high behind the drums pierced a drum and hit Billy's shoulder; seen from the first row [29]
- Billy stood, pointed his sticks up at the crowd and gave the finger [29]
- Providence felt small next to the basketball arenas the band usually played then; these Providence shows were all very good [22]
- A good place to start with 1986 shows; the unusual setlist stands out [26]
- Reviewer rates it the weakest of the three Providence nights [27]
- Solid but not phenomenal, with a 1970s feel and some good cover tunes [28]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd86-03-31.aud.eD.13463.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD>MC>CDR [1]
- **gd1986-03-31.156189.akgc422.davis-murtha-holbrook.flac2448**: taped by Executive Crew; Mike Davis, Kyle Holbrook, Tom Pinney, John Hance, Kenny Davis, Sean Murtha; transferred by Kyle Holbrook; source: Microphones: AKG c422 cardioids (X-Y at 90') |AKG B18 > Nakamichi 550 mic deck Recorder: Sony TC-D5M| Maxell MX 90's no Dolby (2nd in line) Location: OTS… [2]
- **gd1986-03-31.177724.sbd.eaton.miller.repatch.flac1648**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  June 8, 2026; source: SBD > Cassette Master > Reel (Technics) > DAT (Panasonic SV-3800/48k) [5]. Also: Re-patched version of an earlier transfer, from a DAT supplied by Rob Eaton [5]
- **gd1986-03-31.nakcm304.suraci.sbeok.79912.flac16**: taped by Tony Suraci; transferred by Tony Suraci; source: Nak CM304's>Sony D5 [7]. Also: Recorded from the front right corner of the soundboard; this is the 16-bit version, with 24-bit archived on DVDA; Most of the drums segment continued on side B of tape 2 [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Ron Delany Grateful Dead: [1986-04-01 Providence Civic Center, Providence, RI, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1986-04-01-providence-civic-center-providence-ri-usa/) [33]
